content: Oviduct-specific glycoprotein, also referred to as oviductal glycoprotein (OGP), estrogen-dependent oviduct protein (EGP), or mucin-9 (MUC9), is a protein encoded by the OVGP1 gene in humans. This glycoprotein is a large, carbohydrate-rich epithelial protein characterized by numerous O-glycosylation sites, which are located within regions rich in threonine, serine, and proline tandem repeats. The OVGP1 gene shares similarities with members of the mucin and glycosyl hydrolase 18 gene families. Its expression is believed to be regulated in an estrogen-dependent manner. The expression of the OVGP1 gene and the secretion of its protein product occur during the late follicular phase of ovarian development and continue through the early cleavage stages of embryonic development. The protein is secreted by non-ciliated epithelial cells of the oviduct and associates with ovulated oocytes, blastomeres, and the acrosomal regions of spermatozoa. Beyond its presence in the oviduct, OVGP1 has been detected in the mouse ovary, testis, and epididymis, suggesting that it may have roles beyond fertilization. However, it is not detected in the mouse uterus, cervix, vagina, breast, seminal vesicles, or prostate gland. Interestingly, OVGP1 is expressed by the surface epithelium of the endometrium at the time of embryo implantation in mice.
